en.title: Ways to Split All Packages into Balanced Pairs
en.description:
Each package has its own identity, so packages are distinct even when their weights are equal. Split all packages into unordered pairs, using every package exactly once; the absolute weight difference within each pair must be wt. Find the number of complete groupings modulo 1000000007, and return 0 if no complete grouping exists. A clause in the original text about "the number of single pairs" contradicts the main statement and the complete-grouping example whose output is 6; this site explicitly adopts the meaning of the main statement and that example, i.e. pairing up all packages.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n wt; the second line contains the weights. The original snapshot gave no numeric bounds; this site uses 1≤n≤100000, 0≤wt≤10^9, weights 1..10^9.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
hints: When wt is 0, each group of equal weights forms its own perfect matching, so multiply by the odd double factorial. When wt>0, process weights in increasing order: packages still unpaired at the current weight v can only match the next weight v+wt; choose and arrange partners among that weight's remaining identities, multiply by the falling factorial, then subtract the number used.
